Anatomy 04.question: ১) Which of the following is part of respiratory portion of respiratory passage?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The respiratory portion of the respiratory system is the part where gas exchange begins. It includes:

  • Respiratory bronchioles

  • Alveolar ducts

  • Alveolar sacs

  • Alveoli

The conducting portion includes the larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and terminal bronchioles.

High-yield Respiratory histology recall:
Terminal bronchiole → end of conducting portion
Respiratory bronchiole → beginning of respiratory portion

Exam pearl:
“Respiratory bronchiole = first part of respiratory portion.”

Anatomy 04.question: ২) Which type of capillaries are most common?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Continuous capillaries are the most common type of capillary in the body. Their endothelial cells form a relatively continuous lining with small intercellular clefts.

Examples:

  • Muscle

  • Skin

  • Lung

  • CNS (highly specialized continuous capillaries forming the BBB)

Other types:

  • Fenestrated → kidney, endocrine glands, intestinal mucosa

  • Discontinuous/sinusoidal → liver, spleen, bone marrow

Exam pearl:
“Most common capillary = Continuous capillary.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩) Which hormone is not secreted from posterior pituitary?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis) stores and releases two hormones:

  • ADH (vasopressin)

  • Oxytocin

MSH (melanocyte-stimulating hormone) is not secreted from the posterior pituitary. It is primarily associated with the pars intermedia/anterior pituitary.

High-yield Endocrinology recall:
Posterior pituitary → ADH + Oxytocin

Exam pearl:
“Posterior pituitary = ADH + Oxytocin; MSH ≠ posterior pituitary.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৪) Which is the most abundant cell type in respiratory epithelium?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The ciliated columnar cells are the most abundant cells in the typical respiratory epithelium (pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium). Their cilia move the mucus toward the pharynx, helping clear inhaled particles and pathogens.

  • Ciliated columnar cells → most numerous

  • Goblet cells → mucus secretion

  • Brush cells → sensory/receptor function

  • Basal cells → stem/progenitor cells for epithelial renewal

Exam pearl:
“Respiratory epithelium → most abundant = ciliated columnar cells.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৫) Which capillaries are also called sinusoids?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Discontinuous capillaries are also called sinusoids. They have large gaps between endothelial cells and a discontinuous or absent basement membrane, allowing passage of large molecules and even cells.

Examples:

  • Liver → hepatic sinusoids

  • Spleen → splenic sinusoids

  • Bone marrow → sinusoidal capillaries

High-yield Histology recall:
Continuous → muscle, skin, lung
Fenestrated → kidney, endocrine glands, intestine
Discontinuous/sinusoidal → liver, spleen, bone marrow

Exam pearl:
“Sinusoids = discontinuous capillaries.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৬) Which gland is called epiphysis cerebri?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Epiphysis cerebri is another name for the pineal gland, a small endocrine gland located in the epithalamus of the brain.

  • Pineal gland → Epiphysis cerebri

  • Secretes mainly melatonin

  • Plays an important role in regulating the sleep–wake/circadian rhythm

Exam pearl:
“Epiphysis cerebri = Pineal gland.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৭) Which is the most anterior and dilated portion of each nasal cavity?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The nasal vestibule is the most anterior and dilated part of the nasal cavity, located just inside the external nares. It is lined by stratified squamous epithelium and contains vibrissae (nasal hairs).

  • Vestibule → most anterior & dilated part

  • Nares → openings of the nasal cavity

  • Vibrissae → hairs in the nasal vestibule

  • Nasal fossae → the larger internal nasal spaces

Exam pearl:
“Anterior + dilated nasal cavity = Vestibule.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৮) Atherosclerosis occurs in........?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Atherosclerosis primarily occurs in the tunica intima of large and medium-sized arteries, where lipid-rich atheromatous plaques develop.

  • Tunica intima → primary site of atherosclerosis

  • Tunica media → may undergo secondary changes

  • Tunica adventitia → not the primary site

Exam pearl:
“Atheroma = Intima.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৯) Melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH) is produced from.....?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH) is produced primarily by the pars intermedia of the pituitary gland. It is derived from proopiomelanocortin (POMC).

  • Pars intermedia → MSH

  • Pars distalis → GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH

  • Pars tuberalis → part of adenohypophysis surrounding the infundibulum

  • Pars tensa → not a pituitary region

Exam pearl:
“MSH = Pars intermedia.”

Anatomy 04.question: ১০) Which is not a cell of olfactory epithelium?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The olfactory epithelium contains three main cell types:

  1. Olfactory receptor neurons → detect odors

  2. Supporting (sustentacular) cells → provide metabolic and structural support

  3. Basal cells → stem/progenitor cells that regenerate the epithelium

Granular cells are not a component of the olfactory epithelium.

Exam pearl:
“Olfactory epithelium = Olfactory neurons + Supporting cells + Basal cells.”

Anatomy 04.question: ১১) Venae comitantes are especially found in.......?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Venae comitantes are paired veins that accompany arteries, especially the deep arteries of the limbs (extremities). They help venous return through the pumping effect of arterial pulsations and surrounding muscles.

  • Extremities → especially common

  • Usually accompany deep arteries

  • Often occur as two veins accompanying one artery

Exam pearl:
“Venae comitantes = paired veins accompanying deep arteries of limbs.”

Anatomy 04.question: ১২) Which of the following in adenohypophysis is acidophils in nature?
Anatomy 04.exp:
In the adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary), the acidophils are mainly:

  • Somatotrophs → GH

  • Mammotrophs/Lactotrophs → Prolactin

The other listed cells are basophils:

  • Corticotrophs → ACTH

  • Thyrotrophs → TSH

  • Gonadotrophs → FSH & LH

High-yield Pituitary recall:
Acidophils → Somatotroph + Mammotroph
Basophils → Corticotroph + Thyrotroph + Gonadotroph

Exam pearl:
“Mammotroph = acidophil = Prolactin.”

Anatomy 04.question: ১৩) Which is not a paranasal sinuses?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The paranasal sinuses are air-filled cavities in the skull that communicate with the nasal cavity. There are four paired types:

  1. Frontal sinus

  2. Maxillary sinus

  3. Ethmoidal sinuses

  4. Sphenoidal sinus

Palatine is not a paranasal sinus.

Exam pearl:
“Paranasal sinuses = Frontal + Maxillary + Ethmoid + Sphenoid.”

Anatomy 04.question: ১৪) Which is true end artery?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The central artery of the retina is a classic example of a true (anatomical) end artery. It has no significant anastomosis with neighboring arteries, so obstruction can cause sudden and severe retinal ischemia and vision loss.

  • Central artery of retina → true end artery

  • Coronary arteries → functional end arteries

  • Carotid artery → not an end artery

  • Splenic artery → has collateral/anastomotic circulation

High-yield Anatomy recall:
True end artery → central artery of retina
Functional end artery → coronary arteries

Exam pearl:
“Central retinal artery = true end artery.”

Anatomy 04.question: ১৫) Most of the cells of the pars tuberalis are.......?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The pars tuberalis is a part of the adenohypophysis that surrounds the infundibulum. Most of its cells are gonadotrophs, which secrete FSH and LH.

  • Pars tuberalis → predominantly gonadotrophs

  • Gonadotrophs → FSH + LH

  • Somatotrophs → GH

  • Thyrotrophs → TSH

  • Corticotrophs → ACTH

Exam pearl:
“Pars tuberalis = predominantly gonadotrophs.”

Anatomy 04.question: ১৬) What type of circulation is present in kidney?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The kidney has a unique arterial portal system, where blood passes through two successive capillary beds connected by an artery (the efferent arteriole):

Afferent arteriole → Glomerular capillaries → Efferent arteriole → Peritubular capillaries / vasa recta

This arrangement is essential for filtration and reabsorption.

  • Arterial portal system → kidney

  • Hepatic portal system → gastrointestinal tract → liver

  • Pulmonary circulation → heart ↔ lungs

  • Systemic circulation → heart ↔ body tissues

Exam pearl:
“Kidney = arterial portal system.”

Anatomy 04.question: ১৭) How many C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage are there in trachea?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The trachea contains approximately 16–20 C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage. These incomplete rings maintain the patency of the airway while allowing the posterior membranous wall to accommodate the esophagus during swallowing.

  • C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings → 16–20

  • Open posteriorly

  • Trachealis muscle bridges the posterior ends

Exam pearl:
“Trachea = 16–20 C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings.”

Anatomy 04.question: ১৮) Which occupies maximum portion of adenohypophysis?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The pars distalis forms the largest portion of the adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary), accounting for the majority of its volume.

  • Pars distalis → largest part of adenohypophysis

  • Pars tuberalis → surrounds the infundibulum

  • Pars intermedia → small region between pars distalis and neurohypophysis

  • Pars tensa → not a part of the adenohypophysis

Exam pearl:
“Largest part of adenohypophysis = Pars distalis.”

Anatomy 04.question: ১৯) What is the arrangements of fibers in tunica adventitia?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The fibers in the tunica adventitia (tunica externa) of blood vessels are arranged predominantly longitudinally. It is mainly composed of collagen and elastic fibers, providing strength and preventing overdistension.

  • Tunica intima → endothelial lining

  • Tunica media → predominantly circular smooth muscle

  • Tunica adventitia → predominantly longitudinal connective tissue fibers

Exam pearl:
“Tunica media = circular; Tunica adventitia = longitudinal.”

Anatomy 04.question: ২০) The anatomical name for the throat is the......?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The pharynx is the anatomical structure commonly referred to as the throat. It is a muscular tube that serves as a common passage for air and food.

  • Pharynx → throat

  • Larynx → voice box

  • Trachea → windpipe

  • Oesophagus → food pipe

Exam pearl:
“Throat = Pharynx.”

Anatomy 04.question: ২১) The adrenal gland lacks.......?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The adrenal (suprarenal) gland lacks a distinct hilum. Instead, its numerous blood vessels enter through multiple sites on its surface.

  • Adrenal gland → has a capsule

  • Adrenal gland → has rich blood supply

  • Adrenal gland → has supporting connective tissue

  • Hilum → absent

Exam pearl:
“Adrenal gland = no distinct hilum.”

Anatomy 04.question: ২২) Which is not a criteria of an elastic artery?
Anatomy 04.option1: made up of mainly elastic tissue
Anatomy 04.exp:
In elastic arteries such as the aorta, the internal elastic lamina is not distinctly visible because it blends with the numerous elastic lamellae of the tunica media.

Features of elastic arteries:

  • Mainly elastic tissue in tunica media → true

  • Tunica intima is relatively thick → true

  • Tunica adventitia is relatively thin → true

  • Distinct internal elastic lamina → false

High-yield Histology recall:
Elastic artery → numerous elastic lamellae in media → IEL becomes indistinct.

Exam pearl:
“Elastic artery = indistinct internal elastic lamina.”

Anatomy 04.question: ২৩) Clara cells are located in....?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Clara cells, now commonly called club cells, are non-ciliated secretory cells found mainly in the bronchiolar epithelium, especially in terminal and respiratory bronchioles.

Functions include:

  • Secretion of protective components of bronchiolar fluid

  • Detoxification of inhaled substances

  • Regeneration of bronchiolar epithelium

High-yield Respiratory histology recall:
Club (Clara) cells → bronchioles

Exam pearl:
“Clara cells = bronchiolar epithelium.”

Anatomy 04.question: ২৪) Which layer of adrenal cortex occupies maximum space?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The zona fasciculata is the largest and thickest layer of the adrenal cortex, occupying approximately 75% of the cortical volume. Its cells mainly secrete glucocorticoids (especially cortisol).

Adrenal cortex layers from outer → inner:

Zona glomerulosa → Zona fasciculata → Zona reticularis

  • Glomerulosa → mineralocorticoids (aldosterone)

  • Fasciculata → glucocorticoids (cortisol)

  • Reticularis → androgens

Exam pearl:
“Fasciculata = largest adrenal cortical layer.”

Anatomy 04.question: ২৫) Slight dilatation of internal carotid artery is called....?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The carotid sinus is a slight dilatation at the beginning of the internal carotid artery, just above the bifurcation of the common carotid artery.

It contains baroreceptors that detect changes in blood pressure.

  • Carotid sinus → baroreceptor → blood pressure

  • Carotid body → chemoreceptor → O₂, CO₂, H⁺

  • Aortic sinus → dilatation associated with the aortic valve

  • Aortic body → chemoreceptor

Exam pearl:
“Carotid sinus = dilatation + baroreceptor.”

Anatomy 04.question: ২৬) What is the lining epithelium of trachea?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The trachea is lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium, commonly called respiratory epithelium. It contains ciliated columnar cells, goblet cells, basal cells, and other specialized cells.

  • Cilia → move mucus toward the pharynx

  • Goblet cells → secrete mucus

  • Basal cells → epithelial regeneration

Exam pearl:
“Trachea = pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium.”

Anatomy 04.question: ২৭) Zona glomerulosa mainly secrets......?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The zona glomerulosa is the outermost layer of the adrenal cortex and mainly secretes mineralocorticoids, especially aldosterone.

Adrenal cortex layers:

Glomerulosa → Glomerulosa = Aldosterone
Fasciculata → Cortisol
Reticularis → Androgens

Exam pearl:
“GFR = Salt, Sugar, Sex”

  • Glomerulosa → Salt → Aldosterone

  • Fasciculata → Sugar → Cortisol

  • Reticularis → Sex → Androgens

Anatomy 04.question: ২৮) What is the example of fenestrated capillary without diaphragm?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The renal glomerular capillaries are a classic example of fenestrated capillaries without diaphragms. Their fenestrations facilitate rapid filtration of plasma.

  • Renal glomerulus → fenestrated, without diaphragms

  • Intestine → fenestrated with diaphragms

  • Endocrine glands → fenestrated with diaphragms

  • Liver → discontinuous (sinusoidal) capillaries

Exam pearl:
“Fenestrated without diaphragm = renal glomerulus.”

Anatomy 04.question: ২৯) How many layers of respiratory membrane are there?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The respiratory membrane (blood-air barrier) is classically described as having 6 layers:

  1. Alveolar lining fluid/surfactant

  2. Type I pneumocyte

  3. Epithelial basement membrane

  4. Thin interstitial space

  5. Capillary basement membrane

  6. Capillary endothelial cell

Its main function is to allow efficient diffusion of O₂ and CO₂ between the alveolar air and blood.

Exam pearl:
“Respiratory membrane = 6 layers (classical description).”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩০) What is the location of chromaffin cells?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Chromaffin cells are specialized neuroendocrine cells of the adrenal medulla. They are derived from neural crest cells and function like modified sympathetic postganglionic neurons.

They secrete:

  • Adrenaline (epinephrine)

  • Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)

High-yield Adrenal anatomy recall:
Adrenal cortex → steroid hormones
Adrenal medulla → catecholamines from chromaffin cells

Exam pearl:
“Chromaffin cells = adrenal medulla.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩১) Which is true about sinusoids?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Sinusoids (discontinuous capillaries) are wider than typical capillaries and have an irregular, often large-caliber lumen. Their endothelial lining and basement membrane are discontinuous, allowing passage of larger molecules and even cells.

  • Large calibre → true

  • Continuous endothelial lining → false

  • Complete basal lamina → false

  • Regular lumen → false

Examples:
Liver, spleen, and bone marrow

Exam pearl:
“Sinusoids = large, irregular lumen + discontinuous endothelium.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩২) What is the function of type II alveolar cells?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Type II alveolar cells (type II pneumocytes) are specialized secretory cells that produce and release pulmonary surfactant. Surfactant reduces surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse (atelectasis), especially during expiration.

  • Type I pneumocytes → gaseous exchange + thin diffusion barrier

  • Type II pneumocytes → surfactant secretion + regeneration of alveolar epithelium

  • Dust removal → alveolar macrophages

Exam pearl:
“Type II pneumocyte = Surfactant.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩৩) Which is not a feature of artery?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Arteries generally have a thick wall, smaller and more regular lumen, and lack valves. Their tunica media is the thickest layer, not the tunica adventitia.

  • Artery → thick wall

  • Artery → relatively smaller lumen

  • Artery → valves absent

  • Tunica media → thickest layer

  • Tunica adventitia → comparatively thinner than the media in most muscular arteries

Exam pearl:
“Artery = thick media, small lumen, no valves.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩৪) Somatostatin is secreted from which cell of pancreas?
Anatomy 04.exp:
D cells (delta cells) of the islets of Langerhans secrete somatostatin.

  • A/α cells → Glucagon

  • B/β cells → Insulin

  • D/δ cells → Somatostatin

  • PP/γ cells → Pancreatic polypeptide

Exam pearl:
“D = Delta = Somatostatin.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩৫) Which feature involved in protection of the respiratory tract is absent from the digestive tract?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Cilia are a key protective feature of the respiratory tract, where they move mucus and trapped particles toward the pharynx through the mucociliary escalator. They are generally absent from the typical digestive tract lining.

  • Cilia → respiratory tract protection

  • Goblet cells → present in both respiratory and digestive tracts

  • Lymphoid nodules → present in the digestive tract as well

  • Alveoli → respiratory tract, but they are for gas exchange rather than a general protective feature

Exam pearl:
“Mucociliary escalator = cilia + mucus → respiratory defense.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩৬) Which is resistance vessel?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Arterioles are called the resistance vessels because they have a prominent layer of smooth muscle that can constrict or dilate to regulate systemic vascular resistance and blood pressure, as well as control blood flow into capillary beds.

  • Arterioles → resistance vessels

  • Capillaries → exchange vessels

  • Veins → capacitance (reservoir) vessels

  • Large arteries → conducting/distributing vessels

Exam pearl:
“Arterioles = resistance vessels.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩৭) What is the location of coronary sinus?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The coronary sinus is located in the posterior part of the atrioventricular (coronary) groove. It collects most of the venous blood from the myocardium and drains into the right atrium.

  • Coronary sinus → posterior AV groove

  • Drains → right atrium

  • It is the main venous channel of the heart.

Exam pearl:
“Coronary sinus = posterior AV groove → right atrium.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩৮) Which gland has colloidal structure?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The thyroid gland has a characteristic follicular/colloidal structure. Its follicles are lined by simple cuboidal epithelium and contain colloid, which is rich in thyroglobulin, the storage form of thyroid hormone precursors.

  • Thyroid → follicles + colloid

  • Pituitary → cords of endocrine cells

  • Pancreas → acini + islets

  • Parathyroid → cords of chief cells

Exam pearl:
“Colloid-filled follicles = Thyroid gland.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৩৯) Which artery provide arterial supply to heart?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The coronary arteries are the arteries that provide the arterial blood supply to the heart (myocardium). They arise from the ascending aorta, just above the aortic valve.

  • Coronary arteries → supply the heart

  • Carotid arteries → supply head and neck

  • Mesenteric arteries → supply intestines

  • Aortic arch → gives branches but is not itself a coronary supply artery

Exam pearl:
“Heart’s arterial supply = Right & Left coronary arteries.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৪০) How many bronchopulmonary segment are there in right lung?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The right lung classically has 10 bronchopulmonary segments, corresponding to the segmental (tertiary) bronchi.

Right lung segments:

  • Upper lobe → 3

  • Middle lobe → 2

  • Lower lobe → 5

  • Total → 10

Exam pearl:
“Right lung = 10 bronchopulmonary segments.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৪১) Which valve is present in between left atrium & left ventricle?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The bicuspid (mitral) valve is located between the left atrium and left ventricle. It prevents the backflow of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium during ventricular systole.

  • Left atrium → Left ventricle → Mitral/Bicuspid valve

  • Right atrium → Right ventricle → Tricuspid valve

  • Left ventricle → Aorta → Aortic valve

  • Right ventricle → Pulmonary artery → Pulmonary valve

Exam pearl:
“Left AV valve = Mitral/Bicuspid.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৪২) What is the secretion of parafollicular cells of thyroid?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The parafollicular cells (C cells) of the thyroid gland secrete calcitonin. Calcitonin helps lower blood calcium (Ca²⁺) levels, mainly by inhibiting osteoclast-mediated bone resorption.

  • Parafollicular/C cells → Calcitonin

  • Follicular cells → T3 and T4

  • TSH → secreted by anterior pituitary

Exam pearl:
“C cells → Calcitonin.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৪৩) Which bronchopulmonary segment is not present at upper lobe of lung?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The superior (S6) bronchopulmonary segment is a segment of the lower lobe, not the upper lobe.

The upper lobe contains:

  • Apical

  • Posterior

  • Anterior segments

High-yield Anatomy recall:
Upper lobe = Apical + Posterior + Anterior
Lower lobe = Superior + basal segments

Exam pearl:
“Superior segment belongs to the lower lobe.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৪৪) The point where the trachea divides into right and left primary bronchi is a ridge called....?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The carina is a ridge of cartilage at the point where the trachea bifurcates into the right and left primary (main) bronchi.

  • Trachea → Carina → Right & Left main bronchi

  • Located approximately at the level of the sternal angle (T4–T5).

  • It is highly sensitive and stimulation can trigger a cough reflex.

Exam pearl:
“Tracheal bifurcation ridge = Carina.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৪৫) How many pulmonary vein enters into left atrium?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Normally, four pulmonary veins enter the left atrium:

  • 2 right pulmonary veins → superior & inferior

  • 2 left pulmonary veins → superior & inferior

They carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

Exam pearl:
“Left atrium receives 4 pulmonary veins.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৪৬) Which is not one of the major targets of PTH?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The major targets of parathyroid hormone (PTH) are:

  • Bone → osteoblasts/osteocytes indirectly stimulate osteoclast activity

  • Kidney (renal tubules) → increases Ca²⁺ reabsorption and decreases phosphate reabsorption

  • Intestine → indirectly increases Ca²⁺ absorption via activation of vitamin D in the kidney

The bile duct is not a major target of PTH.

Exam pearl:
PTH → Bone + Kidney + Intestine (indirectly).

Anatomy 04.question: ৪৭) Where there is no capillary?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The cornea is avascular, meaning it contains no blood capillaries. It receives oxygen mainly by diffusion from the atmosphere through the tear film and nutrients from the aqueous humor and limbal vessels.

  • Cornea → avascular

  • Liver → rich sinusoidal capillary network

  • Lung → extensive pulmonary capillary network

  • Kidney → extensive glomerular and peritubular capillary networks

Exam pearl:
“Cornea = avascular tissue.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৪৮) Which region of the adrenal gland is involved in Addison's disease?
Anatomy 04.exp:
Addison's disease is primary adrenal insufficiency, usually due to destruction of the adrenal cortex. This causes deficiency of aldosterone, cortisol, and adrenal androgens.

However, the question asks for a specific region of the adrenal gland. Among the given options, zona glomerulosa is part of the affected adrenal cortex and is responsible for aldosterone secretion.

  • Zona glomerulosa → aldosterone

  • Zona fasciculata → cortisol

  • Zona reticularis → androgens

  • Adrenal medulla → catecholamines

Important correction: Addison's disease affects the entire adrenal cortex, not only the zona glomerulosa.

Exam pearl:
“Addison's = adrenal cortex failure → ↓ cortisol + ↓ aldosterone + ↓ androgens.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৪৯) What is the location of epiglottis?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The epiglottis is a leaf-shaped elastic cartilage located at the entrance of the larynx. During swallowing, it helps prevent food and liquid from entering the airway.

  • Epiglottis → larynx

  • Trachea → airway below the larynx

  • Pharynx → common passage for food and air

  • Bronchi → branches of the trachea

Exam pearl:
“Epiglottis = laryngeal inlet.”

Anatomy 04.question: ৫০) A flaplike structure that covers the larynx during swallowing is called....?
Anatomy 04.exp:
The epiglottis is a leaf-shaped, flap-like structure made of elastic cartilage that covers the laryngeal inlet during swallowing, helping prevent food and liquid from entering the respiratory tract.

  • Epiglottis → protects airway during swallowing

  • Larynx → voice box

  • Trachea → windpipe

  • Carina → ridge at tracheal bifurcation

Exam pearl:
“Epiglottis = protective flap over the laryngeal inlet.”
